messages.content: You are one member of a parallel architecture inquiry. Return only the contracted JSON. Produce executable mechanisms, APIs, state transitions, and verification rules; do not propose organizational process or prose-only governance.

Evidence: 84 Claude sessions in five days manually performed environment diagnosis, repository archaeology, architecture reconstruction, research synthesis, Lean proof work, refactors, tests, memory/skill creation, and repeated failure analysis. A transcript audit counted 2,067 direct mutations versus 190 subagent dispatches and about 30% human corrections. Prior harness research specifies carrier adapters with zero substrate intelligence, append-only prompt/tool/result capture, projected memory/context, deterministic tools, governed consolidation only after results, session heartbeats, work claim/settle, and context-compaction continuity. The existing free-compute-dev seed has deterministic resolver -> context -> model edit -> apply -> test -> feedback rounds -> expensive escalation, but only one task and no autonomous intake/decomposition/fanout/tool navigation/isolation/integration/memory. The existing LISS cheapest-sufficient fabric just demonstrated 24/24 schema-verified jobs at 24.45 useful jobs/min across Gemini and GitHub Models, with OpenRouter fallback and Claude available. Future volunteer CPU/GPU endpoints can join over Tailscale. The target is a Union-owned software-production fabric that receives territories/problems and keeps observing, decomposing, executing, verifying, integrating, and learning without a Codex or Claude conversation carrying the work.

Your bounded question: Design scheduling across heterogeneous free cloud endpoints, Claude, scripts, and future Tailscale GPU workers, optimizing expected cost to verified resolution.

State what is absent from the current seed, give a concrete design, and name a smallest real vertical slice.

structured_output.absentMechanism: The seed has one deterministic execution path with no capability registry, no cost model, no concurrent task isolation, no work queue with claim/settle, and no empirical routing memory. Every task implicitly targets one endpoint; there is no mechanism to ask "what is the cheapest endpoint that can verifiably complete this task type?" nor to track which endpoint succeeded or failed on prior instances of each task class.
design: Capability registry: each endpoint publishes a static manifest (model_id, supported_tools, context_window_tokens, cost_per_1k_tokens, rate_limit_rpm) plus a live heartbeat (queue_depth, tokens_remaining_this_minute). Registry stored as append-only JSONL, compacted on read.

Task typing: each work item carries a RequirementVector {needs_code_execution: bool, min_context_tokens: int, complexity: enum[trivial|code|research|proof], language: str[]}. Derived from task metadata at intake, not inferred by the scheduler.

Expected cost model: cost(endpoint, task) = (tokens_estimated * cost_per_token) / P_success(endpoint, task.complexity). P_success initialized to 1.0 and updated via Bayesian beta prior after each settle event.

Scheduler loop: filter registry to endpoints satisfying RequirementVector, sort ascending by cost(endpoint, task), claim top candidate with TTL=2*estimated_duration, dispatch, await heartbeat or timeout.

Claim/settle: append {task_id, endpoint_id, claimed_at, ttl} to claims.jsonl; on settle append {task_id, outcome, tokens_used, verified: bool}. Scheduler re-scans for expired unclaimed tasks on each tick.
Tailscale workers: register via the same manifest endpoint over Tailscale with identical JSON schema; scheduler treats them as any other endpoint with no special-casing.

Escalation: if top-k cheapest endpoints all return verified=false, RequirementVector.complexity is promoted one tier and the scheduler retries from the filter step with a human-escalation terminal state at max tier.
firstVerticalSlice: Write capability-registry.jsonl with two entries: Gemini-Flash (cost_per_1k=0, needs_code_execution=false) and Claude-Haiku (cost_per_1k=0.0025, needs_code_execution=true).
Add needs_code_execution: bool to existing task schema; default false for all 24 existing LISS benchmark tasks.
Implement scheduler as a single Python function: filter registry by needs_code_execution, pick min cost_per_1k, call existing carrier adapter, write claim and settle records to JSONL.
Run the existing 24-job LISS benchmark through the scheduler with no other changes; record per-job endpoint_id, tokens_used, verified.
Compare total cost (sum of tokens_used * cost_per_1k) to the all-Claude-Haiku baseline on the same 24 jobs and confirm at least one job routed to Gemini-Flash.
failureModes: Stale heartbeat: endpoint appears available but is rate-limited; claim times out after TTL, task requeues with exponential backoff.

Cold P_success prior: all endpoints start at 1.0, masking real capability differences; require minimum 5 settled tasks per (endpoint, complexity) cell before trusting empirical estimates over the capability filter alone.

RequirementVector misclassification: task marked needs_code_execution=false but actually requires execution; cheap endpoint returns hallucinated output that passes schema check but fails downstream functional verification.
Claim race on shared JSONL: two scheduler instances read the same unclaimed task before either write is flushed; mitigate with a file lock or monotonic claim sequence ID.
Runaway escalation: task fails at every complexity tier, exhausts the endpoint list, and loops with no defined terminal human-escalation path.
structured_output.successMetric: Over 50 consecutive schema-verified settlements with at least two distinct endpoint types exercised: mean(tokens_used * cost_per_1k) per verified task is strictly lower than the all-Claude-Haiku baseline on the same corpus, and P_success(Gemini-Flash, trivial) >= 0.80 after 20 trivial tasks settle.
